order: Pitch some ideas now, learn from analytics and trends (Commander, via Claude Code)
theme: trend × impossible what-if; payoff at 0:00; 30–35 s

pitches.title: What if GTA 6 physics were *real* for 5 seconds?
pitches.cover: A 100 KM/H CRASH HITS LIKE A 13-STOREY FALL
pitches.frame1: 0:00, mid-air: a city delivery van has bounced off a lamp post like rubber and is spinning 15 m above a sunny boulevard; drivers stare up. Title over it. Counter: GAME PHYSICS · 5.0 s

beats.what: The van is already airborne; a taxi behind it hits the kerb and pinballs off three parked cars, unscratched
A scooter rider clips a bin, ragdolls 20 m in a cartoon arc and lands sitting in a cafe chair (comic beat, no injury)
A pickup hits a boat ramp at 100 km/h and flies 79 m across the marina, peaking 20 m up, landing on a yacht that bounces it back
Traffic on a highway overpass chains into a bouncing pile, cars launched over the railings into the sky
The 5 s end: real physics snaps back while hundreds of cars hang mid-air; they stop bouncing and crumple into roofs and the bay
Close on one car: a real 100 km/h stop crushes it like a 39 m drop; then hard cut back to the spinning van

pitches.law: Kinetic energy: a car at 100 km/h (27.8 m/s) carries the energy of a drop from h = v²/2g = 39 m (~13 storeys). In game physics collisions are elastic: a 45° ramp at 27.8 m/s throws it v²/g = 79 m, peak 20 m.
pitches.dramatization: For 5 s collisions are perfectly elastic and falls are harmless (game rules); everything after uses real physics.
why: GTA 6 video: 6,590 views and 38.8% watched in full, 3–7× our other recent posts; ~55% of its search traffic was 'gta 6'
GTA 6 launched 2026-11-19, largest entertainment launch ever (Forbes); 39M+ PS5 players in 4 days
Ladder 5 s → snap-back mirrors the 👍 gravity-flip structure
pitches.risk: IP: the picture must be our own city and cars, with no Rockstar logos, map, characters or HUD; 'GTA 6' only in title/caption. Gore risk on the snap-back: keep cars empty or people out of frame. Could be the first episode of a series ('If games were real', Ep. 1) to win follows.

reuse: gravity-flip lift system for airborne cars
new: elastic bounce solver for cars (simple rigid-body bounces)

pitches.title: What if the air got 10× *thicker* for 5 seconds?
pitches.cover: IN 10× THICKER AIR A LIGHT BREEZE HITS LIKE A HURRICANE
pitches.frame1: 0:00, a market street is already being swept: a 40 km/h breeze now hits like 126 km/h, awnings rip loose, a fruit stall tumbles, people lean into it holding hats. Counter: AIR DENSITY · ×10

beats.what: Awnings tear off, oranges stream sideways, a man's umbrella drags him along like a kite (comic beat)
A taxiing airliner gets 10× the lift and leaps off the runway at walking pace, nose up
Roofs peel off in a row, trampolines and bins fly, trees bend flat
The sea surface whips into huge spray walls; boats are shoved across the harbour
Falling debris and a skydiver drift down slowly like in syrup (terminal speed ÷3.2)
Earth from space: the whole sky haze-thick and white as the 5 s ends; hard cut to the market

pitches.law: Drag and lift scale with air density: F = ½ρv²C·A. At ρ ×10, a wind of v feels like √10·v ≈ 3.16v; 40 km/h → 126 km/h (hurricane is ≥119 km/h). Terminal speed scales 1/√10 ≈ ÷3.2.
pitches.dramatization: The density jumps everywhere at once; we ignore the pressure shock on bodies (eardrums) so no one is hurt.
why: Mirror of the 👍 'air vanished' and 'X becomes … for 5 seconds' pattern (7 of 7 recent 👍)
Planes leaping into the sky echoes the gravity-flip 👍 'planes into space'
Cheap: reuses city, bay, planes and clouds
pitches.risk: No trend hook: expect our usual 1–2K unless the hook lands at 0:00. Fix: open on the most violent frame and put the hurricane number in the cover.

new: wind field that drags props and awnings
a coastal market set (new place for variety)

pitches.title: What if everything got 10× *bigger*, except you?
pitches.cover: MAKE A BRIDGE 10× BIGGER AND IT'S 10× TOO WEAK
pitches.frame1: 0:00, a suspension bridge already 10× its size is sagging and snapping cables over a river; tiny people on the bank look up. Counter: SIZE · ×10

beats.what: Cables snap one by one, the deck buckles under its own weight and folds into the river
A clock tower, now 400 m tall, cracks at the base and topples across the square (people safe at the edges)
A 10 m pigeon can't fly (wings too weak) and waddles; a giant dog lies down, legs buckling, confused (comic beat)
Towers 3 km tall crumble from the bottom up like sandcastles
Even mountains slump: a peak sags and avalanches flow down
Earth itself 10× wider: its gravity ×10 pulls the Moon in; hard cut to the bridge

pitches.law: Square-cube law: scale by 10 and weight grows ×1,000 (volume) while strength grows ×100 (cross-section), so stress grows ×10, far past any building's safety margin (typically 1.5–2×).
pitches.dramatization: Everything scales instantly except people; the mountain and planet beats simplify the geology.
why: Novel, impossible, whole-world premise that passes the 'wait, WHAT?' test
Visible physical destruction in new places every beat (👍 pattern)
pitches.risk: Most expensive build (giant scaled sets, buckling structures). Fix: keep it to 5 shots plus the orbit end, reuse city.js towers with a scale and collapse pass.
